cards.text: Abram is the man God called to go to a land He would show him (Genesis 12:1), and Pharaoh, Egypt's king, has just had his men send Abram away with his wife and everything he owns (Genesis 12:20). So Abram goes up out of Egypt into the Negev, and his nephew Lot is with him (Genesis 12:5). Friend, getting walked to the door by Pharaoh's men isn't a send-off, that's a BOUNCER.

cards.question: Abram leaves Egypt a whole lot richer than he showed up. What has he become extremely wealthy in?

cards.text: From the Negev, Abram travels from place to place toward Bethel. He comes back to the spot between Bethel and Ai where his tent stood before, where he had built the altar.

cards.question: Back at the altar he built between Bethel and Ai, Abram calls on the name of the LORD.

cards.text: Now Lot's not traveling light either. He's got flocks and herds and tents of his own, and friend, when I left the bakery that sold me out of a bin, everything I owned was a price sticker that said 25 CENTS.

cards.question: The land has plenty of room for Abram and Lot to stay together with everything they own.
With the land stretched thin, discord breaks out between the herdsmen of Abram and the herdsmen of ___.

cards.text: And it's not just Abram and Lot out there. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites are living in the land too.
So Abram says to Lot, "Please let there be no contention between you and me, or between your herdsmen and my herdsmen."

cards.question: Abram's reason for keeping the peace with Lot: after all, they are ___.

cards.text: Then Abram makes Lot an offer: "Is not the whole land before you? Now separate yourself from me." Friend, that's handing somebody the TV remote AND the good seat on the couch.

cards.question: Abram tells Lot the two of them should separate. If Lot goes to the left, which way will Abram go?

cards.text: With first pick in his hands, Lot looks out over the whole plain of the Jordan, all the way to Zoar, a town. Friend, give me first pick and I'm squinting at every option like it owes me MONEY.

cards.question: What does Lot see when he looks out over the plain of the Jordan?
The writer says the well-watered plain of the Jordan is like the garden of the LORD. What land does he also compare it to?
The writer adds a note about Sodom and Gomorrah, two cities. When Lot looks out over the plain of the Jordan, the LORD has already destroyed them.
Lot chooses the whole plain of the Jordan for himself and sets out toward the ___.

cards.text: And just like that, Abram and Lot part company. Abram lives in the land of Canaan, and Lot settles in the cities of the plain, pitching his tent toward Sodom.

cards.question: The men of Sodom, the city Lot pitched his tent toward, were wicked, sinning greatly against the LORD.

cards.text: After Lot has gone, the LORD speaks to Abram. He tells Abram to lift up his eyes and look north and south and east and west.

cards.question: The LORD says all the land Abram can see, He will give to Abram and his ___ forever.

cards.text: Then the LORD says He'll make Abram's offspring like the dust of the earth: if anyone could count the dust, they could count Abram's offspring. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer counting dust as it fell, and I never got anywhere close to finishing.
And the LORD tells Abram to get up and walk around the land, through its length and breadth, for He will give it to him.
So Abram moves his tent and goes to live near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron. Abram and that tent are like me and this gold base: wherever I go, it comes WITH me.

cards.question: At his new home near the Oaks of Mamre at Hebron, what does Abram build?

cards.text: Abram's settled in near those oaks for now, friend, but this story is far from finished.
